refnamediv.refpurpose: Query or control the realtime scheduling policy service

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: systemd-rtwatch may be used to query and control systemd-rtwatchd.service8, the service that hands out realtime scheduling and high priority to threads of unprivileged processes. It communicates with the service via its io.systemd.RTWatch Varlink interface.

refsect1.title: Commands

listitem.para: Show the policy the service enforces and its current state. This is the default if no command is specified.

List the threads the service currently made realtime or high priority, together with the process and thread they belong to, the unit of the process, its command line, and the name of the thread. Unprivileged users only see threads of their own processes.

Make the main thread of the specified process (or the thread specified with --thread=) realtime at the specified priority. The process must have set the hard limit of RLIMIT_RTTIME appropriately, see systemd-rtwatchd.service8.

Set the nice level of the main thread of the specified process (or of the thread specified with --thread=) to the specified value. Since nice levels are usually negative, separate the arguments from the options with --, for example systemd-rtwatch make-high-priority -- 4711 -10.
Demote all threads the service handed out realtime scheduling or high priority to.
Demote all realtime threads of the system (except for those owned by root, unless the service is configured otherwise).
Temporarily demote all known threads, and promote them again.

refsect1.para: reset-known, reset-all, suspend and resume require privileges, and are authorized via polkit, see systemd-rtwatchd.service8.

listitem.para: Use with make-realtime and make-high-priority to operate on the specified thread of the process, instead of its main thread. Takes a kernel thread ID.

refsect1.title: Exit status
refsect1.para: On success, 0 is returned, a non-zero failure code otherwise.
